channel.title: Bilan du monde
channel.description: World news in five minutes, every morning.

item.title: Saturday, November 14, 2026 · Ukraine: Europeans set to join next round of talks
item.description:
• According to US envoys, Europeans will take part in the next round of talks on Ukraine, but Moscow has not confirmed it.
  • Sébastien Lecornu opened a month of talks with civil service unions on Friday; they are keeping their November 17 strike, which the CFDT union has now joined.
  • In Guinea, clashes between security forces and gold miners left ten dead near Siguiri.
  • At COP31, three public finance institutions aim to raise $10 billion for climate projects by 2030.
  • France's rugby team beat South Africa 21-19 at the Stade de France.

item.title: Friday, November 13, 2026 · Jensen Huang steps down at Nvidia, Colette Kress takes over on an interim basis
item.description:
• Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down as head of the chip giant on Thursday, effective immediately; chief financial officer Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO.
  • Nvidia shares plunged about 13% at the open on Wall Street after the announcement.
  • US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin before joining Volodymyr Zelensky in Dublin.
  • In football, France suffered their first defeat of the Zidane era, losing 3-1 to Italy in Milan.

item.title: Thursday, November 12, 2026 · Ukraine: Moscow and Kyiv agree on a large prisoner exchange
item.description:
• Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi ended on Wednesday with a deal on a large prisoner exchange, but no progress towards peace.
  • Emmanuel Macron led his last Armistice Day ceremony as head of state, amid a row over commemorations in schools.
  • At the COP31 summit in Antalya, António Guterres called for a climate justice pact.
  • Global fossil CO2 emissions are set to fall by 0.41% in 2026, according to the Global Carbon Budget.
  • In Paris, the CAC 40 rose 0.66% in a quiet session, with 11 November a public holiday.

item.title: Wednesday, November 11, 2026 · Ukraine: Russians, Ukrainians and Americans meet in Abu Dhabi
item.description:
• Russian, Ukrainian and US delegations opened a new round of peace talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday, mediated by Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
  • In France, teachers, high-school pupils and university students were again called out on strike on Tuesday to demand more resources.
  • The Paris stock exchange gained 0.55% as oil prices fell, while chipmaker Nexperia says it can no longer keep up with demand.
  • In the Women's Champions League, it was a tough night for the Paris clubs: PSG lost 1-2 to Bayern and Paris FC lost 3-0 in Madrid.

item.title: Tuesday, November 10, 2026 · Minimum wage to rise 1.6% from December 1
item.description:
• Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday, November 9, an early 1.6% rise in the minimum wage on December 1, to €1,502 net a month; the CGT union is calling a strike on November 17.
  • In Poland, the Kraków gunman, who killed six people on Saturday, died in hospital; authorities describe a far-right-inspired attack.
  • Europeans are set to join the US-brokered talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi, despite Kremlin objections.
  • COP31 opened in Antalya amid a dispute over climate finance, while the WMO confirms that 2015-2026 will be the warmest twelve-year period on record.
  • In Paris, the CAC 40 gained 1.16% on Monday as oil prices fell; on Wall Street, Nvidia lost about 4% after an investigation into its CEO was opened.

item.title: Monday, November 9, 2026 · Israel: Eisenkot tasked with forming the government
item.description:
• Israel: Gadi Eisenkot received the mandate on Sunday to form the next government, instead of Benjamin Netanyahu.
  • Ukraine: Russia steps up its strikes ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks on Tuesday.
  • In France, unions and employers meet at Matignon today for a social conference on wages.
  • COP31 opens today in Antalya; in sailing, Tom Laperche wins the Route du Rhum in record time.

item.title: Sunday, November 8, 2026 · Wall Street: the Nasdaq 100 has its worst day since 2020
item.description:
• The Nasdaq 100 had its worst session since 2020 on Thursday (−6.36%), despite a much stronger-than-expected US jobs report.
  • Israel: Gadi Eisenkot, recommended by 67 lawmakers, was due to receive the mandate to form the next government on Sunday.
  • In France, unions and employers meet at Matignon on Monday for a social conference on wages.
  • The COP31 climate conference opens on Monday, November 9, in Antalya, Türkiye.
